digest.headline: Découplage des architectures décisionnelles et modélisation énergétique avancent la généralisation et l'efficacité des systèmes d'IA
digest.overview: Les avancées du 2026-11-06 mettent en lumière des progrès structurants pour les agents autonomes, l'optimisation des LLM et la robotique. Les travaux sur les architectures découplées et les modèles prédictifs partagés dominent, tandis que des cadres théoriques émergent pour évaluer et améliorer la robustesse des systèmes en production.

highlights.title: Architectures découplées pour agents et décisions
highlights.text: Le papier DPDM introduit une séparation entre la représentation sémantique (LLM) et la prédiction conditionnelle (modèle partagé gelé) pour les agents décisionnels, améliorant la généralisation sur 50 benchmarks sans réentraînement. Parallèlement, Drex propose des modèles décisionnels non auto-régressifs (8B-35B paramètres) combinant fine-tuning supervisé et RL, atteignant 67,52% sur Decision Index 0.4.1. Ces approches répondent au besoin de cohérence et d'efficacité dans les systèmes autonomes.

highlights.title: Optimisation énergétique et accélération de l'inférence
highlights.text: La *SIMPLE Law* modélise analytiquement le coût énergétique des LLM avec une précision 3x supérieure aux méthodes existantes (R²=0,969), sans calibration par modèle. D3D accélère l'inférence via un drafter diffusion découplé et un pruning progressif, offrant un speedup de 5x à 7,48x sur Qwen3. StrataFlux optimise quant à lui l'inférence low-bit en récupérant la précision via un streaming sélectif depuis la mémoire hiérarchique, crucial pour le déploiement sur hardware contraint.

highlights.title: Robustesse et évaluation des agents IA
highlights.text: Le cadre *Decision-Value* pour les moniteurs de redémarrage des agents montre que la précision seule est insuffisante, introduisant des critères décisionnels (suffisance, audit) pour optimiser les redémarrages. EvoMemState remplace les mémoires factuelles par des états relationnels dynamiques, améliorant la robustesse des agents personnalisés. Ces travaux adressent des lacunes critiques dans l'évaluation et la fiabilité des systèmes autonomes.

highlights.title: Fondations pour la robotique et les modèles incarnés
highlights.text: SLA propose un modèle *Spatial-Language-Action* pré-entraîné en continu pour aligner représentations 2D/3D et actions robotiques, tandis qu'Open-HumanScale offre une recette ouverte pour entraîner des modèles fondés sur 50k heures d'expérience humaine et robotique. DreamFree distille un encodeur visuel prédictif pour un contrôle robotique en temps réel (11Hz) sans génération vidéo itérative, marquant des étapes vers des *Embodied Foundation Models* transférables.

highlights.title: Interprétabilité et limites expérimentales
highlights.text: L'étude sur l'information intégrée (φ) révèle que des symétries cachées ou unités exclues limitent la précision expérimentale, même avec un grand nombre d'essais. Une synthèse exhaustive sur la *mechanistic interpretability* couvre les méthodes d'extraction de features et de vérification causale, soulignant son rôle pour la sécurité IA. Ces travaux éclairent les défis théoriques et pratiques de l'interprétabilité.

highlights.title: Risques en production et optimisation des benchmarks
highlights.text: Une étude révèle que 41% des réparations de code LLM après migrations d'API passent les tests standards mais échouent sur des entrées marginales, exposant des risques critiques pour les systèmes en production. BestRand propose une méthode de compression de benchmarks réduisant les erreurs d'estimation de 50% et les coûts de 48%, tout en maintenant la précision. Ces contributions adressent des enjeux concrets de fiabilité et d'efficacité.

digest.trend: Les architectures découplées et les modèles prédictifs partagés s'imposent comme des leviers clés pour la généralisation et l'efficacité, tandis que l'optimisation énergétique et la robustesse des systèmes autonomes deviennent des priorités. La robotique et les modèles incarnés progressent vers des fondations transférables, mais les défis d'interprétabilité et de fiabilité en production restent centraux.

items.title: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents
items.summary: Agent decisions depend on empirical relationships that deployment observations reveal and task descriptions alone may leave unresolved. We introduce Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM), an architecture that formulates heterogeneous agent decisions as conditional prediction with a shared pretrained learner. Language models provide semantic representations of current and historical records, while a general-purpose conditional predictor predicts task-defined targets from the represented evidence. Pretraining supplies reusable inference capability; deployment evidence instantiates problem-specific predictions without updating either model's neural parameters. Tool judgments, candidate preferences, and reasoning assessments share an evidence-and-query interface, with predictions mapped to choices by a decision rule. This architecture establishes complementary sources of agent capability: semantic knowledge acquired through language pretraining and empirical inference acquired through structured-data pretraining. A single frozen LimiX-2 predictor serves all five task categories. With Qwen3.5-27B as the semantic encoder, DPDM raises mean accuracy across 50 benchmarks from 78.80% with few-shot prompting to 84.92% under their respective evaluated history budgets, and reaches 82.33% with identical histories and queries. On ToolPRMBench's BFCL and ToolSandbox tasks, absolute accuracy gains are 34.26% and 28.87%, respectively, at the methods' respective evaluated history budgets. Accuracy improves as history grows. With identical imbalanced histories, mean balanced accuracy improves by an absolute 14.51% across five reasoning-step assessment tasks and four encoders. DPDM makes learning from experience an independently improvable foundation-model capability, creating a shared route for advances in conditional prediction to improve decisions across agent tasks.
items.tldr: Architecture DPDM pour agents décisionnels, séparant la représentation sémantique (LLM) de la prédiction conditionnelle (modèle partagé) pour améliorer la généralisation sur 50 benchmarks sans réentraînement, avec un seul prédicteur gelé (LimiX-2).

deep_analysis.probleme: Le problème abordé concerne la prise de décision par des agents IA dans des contextes où les descriptions de tâches seules ne suffisent pas à résoudre les ambiguïtés. Les relations empiriques, révélées par les observations en phase de déploiement, sont souvent négligées ou difficiles à intégrer dynamiquement sans réentraînement coûteux des modèles.

methode.approche_generale: DPDM (Decoupled Predictive Decision Making) propose une architecture découplée où un encodeur sémantique (un modèle de langage comme Qwen3.5-27B) et un prédicteur conditionnel partagé (LimiX-2) collaborent. Le modèle de langage génère des représentations sémantiques des observations historiques et actuelles, tandis que le prédicteur conditionnel, préentraîné sur des données structurées, infère les cibles définies par la tâche à partir de ces représentations.

details_techniques.pretraitement: Le prédicteur conditionnel est préentraîné pour acquérir une capacité d'inférence réutilisable, tandis que l'encodeur sémantique est figé (frozen). Aucune mise à jour des paramètres neuronaux n'est nécessaire lors du déploiement, ce qui permet une adaptation rapide aux nouvelles observations.
details_techniques.interface_unifiee: Les jugements d'outils, préférences de candidats et évaluations de raisonnement partagent une interface commune basée sur des preuves (evidence) et des requêtes (query). Les prédictions sont ensuite mappées à des choix via une règle de décision.
details_techniques.sources_de_capacite: L'architecture combine deux sources complémentaires : la connaissance sémantique issue du préentraînement du modèle de langage et l'inférence empirique acquise via le préentraînement sur des données structurées.

resultats.benchmarks_generaux: DPDM améliore la précision moyenne sur 50 benchmarks, passant de 78,80% avec un *few-shot prompting* à 84,92% en utilisant les budgets d'historique évalués. Avec des historiques et requêtes identiques, la précision atteint 82,33%.
resultats.taches_specifiques: Sur ToolPRMBench (BFCL et ToolSandbox), les gains absolus de précision sont de 34,26% et 28,87% respectivement, aux budgets d'historique évalués. L'ajout d'historique améliore systématiquement les performances.
resultats.raisonnement: Avec des historiques déséquilibrés identiques, la précision équilibrée moyenne s'améliore de 14,51% absolus sur cinq tâches d'évaluation de raisonnement et quatre encodeurs.

limites.dependance_aux_donnees: La performance dépend fortement de la qualité et de la représentativité des données d'historique utilisées pour l'inférence conditionnelle. Des biais dans ces données pourraient se répercuter sur les décisions.
limites.generalisation: Bien que le prédicteur soit partagé entre plusieurs tâches, il n'est pas clair si cette approche généralise à des domaines très éloignés de ceux utilisés lors du préentraînement.
limites.interpretabilite: L'architecture repose sur des modèles complexes (comme Qwen3.5-27B), ce qui peut rendre difficile l'interprétation des décisions prises, notamment pour des applications critiques.

deep_analysis.verdict: Cette approche mérite une attention particulière pour son potentiel à améliorer significativement la prise de décision des agents IA sans réentraînement coûteux, mais son applicabilité à grande échelle et dans des contextes variés reste à valider.

items.title: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference
items.summary: Generative AI is billed per token, yet tokens are not equally expensive. Each token enters the KV-cache and raises the cost of those that follow, so energy grows non-linearly along a sequence whose tokens look identical. No analytical model states what a token costs, and the most accurate SOTA model is a fit, not a law: it absorbs architecture into fitted coefficients, requiring per-LLM fitting. We derive closed-form expressions of the computational and memory-access complexity of LLM inference in terms of architectural hyperparameters, covering MHA and GQA, and compare a family of analytical models of increasing granularity. From these, we obtain the SIMPLE Inference Model to Predict LLMs Energy (SIMPLE), a four-parameter law that separates prefill from decode, and decode into KV-cache cost and next-token computation. Over traces of 13 dense LLMs from six families on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, it attains R2 = 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE, 3.1-3.5x below the SOTA, without per-LLM calibration. The SIMPLE law explains as well as predicts: prefill energy grows quadratically with the hidden dimension, so larger LLMs suffer most from long inputs; and more aggressive GQA KV grouping reduces the per-token energy by up to 3x relative to standard MHA. Increasing the reasoning token budget pushes output length beyond the analytically derived energy minimum, driving super-linear energy growth; although accuracy grows with the budget, energy grows faster, so Intelligence per Joule peaks at an intermediate budget and falls by up to 3.14x across a 4.0x reasoning-budget range. Agentic serving raises energy per request by 13.0x relative to non-agentic ones, driven by the growth of both the prefill and the KV-cache terms with input length; while prefix caching removes most of the prefill cost (-93%), the KV-cache term is unaffected, so even a cached agentic request costs 4.8x more.
items.tldr: SIMPLE Law modélise analytiquement le coût énergétique de l'inférence des LLM en fonction des paramètres architecturaux, offrant une précision 3x supérieure aux modèles existants (R²=0.969, MAPE=11.97%) sans calibration par modèle.

deep_analysis.probleme: La publication aborde l'absence de modèle analytique précis pour estimer le coût énergétique de l'inférence des grands modèles de langage (LLM). Actuellement, les coûts sont facturés par token sans distinction de leur complexité réelle, alors que chaque token ajouté augmente non-linéairement la consommation énergétique en raison de la croissance du cache KV (clés-valeurs). Les modèles existants reposent sur des ajustements empiriques plutôt que sur des lois fondamentales, limitant leur généralisation.
deep_analysis.methode: Les auteurs dérivent des expressions en forme fermée pour la complexité computationnelle et l'accès mémoire lors de l'inférence des LLM, en fonction des hyperparamètres architecturaux. Ils couvrent les mécanismes d'attention multi-têtes (MHA) et de groupement de requêtes (GQA), puis comparent une famille de modèles analytiques de granularité croissante. Le modèle SIMPLE (SIMPLE Inference Model to Predict LLMs Energy) est proposé, avec seulement quatre paramètres, séparant les phases de préremplissage (*prefill*) et de décodage (*decode*), tout en distinguant le coût du cache KV et celui du calcul du token suivant. Ce modèle évite un calibrage spécifique par LLM.
deep_analysis.resultats: Le modèle SIMPLE atteint un coefficient de détermination R² de 0,969 et une erreur absolue moyenne en pourcentage (MAPE) de 11,97 % sur des traces de 13 LLM denses issus de six familles, exécutés sur des GPU NVIDIA H100. Ces performances surpassent l'état de l'art de 3,1 à 3,5 fois sans calibration par modèle. Les résultats révèlent que l'énergie du préremplissage croît quadratiquement avec la dimension cachée, pénalisant davantage les grands modèles pour les entrées longues. Le groupement GQA réduit jusqu'à 3 fois l'énergie par token par rapport à MHA. Enfin, l'augmentation du budget de tokens de raisonnement entraîne une croissance super-linéaire de l'énergie, avec un pic d'efficacité énergétique (Intelligence par Joule) à un budget intermédiaire.
deep_analysis.limites: Le contenu disponible ne précise pas les hypothèses sous-jacentes du modèle SIMPLE (ex : validité pour des architectures non denses ou des GPU autres que H100). Les traces utilisées pour la validation pourraient ne pas couvrir tous les cas d'usage réels, notamment les scénarios extrêmes ou les modèles hybrides. Enfin, l'impact des optimisations logicielles (ex : quantification, sparsité) n'est pas abordé, ce qui pourrait limiter la portée des conclusions.
deep_analysis.verdict: Cette publication mérite une attention particulière pour son approche analytique rigoureuse et ses implications pratiques sur l'optimisation énergétique des LLM, bien que des validations supplémentaires soient nécessaires pour en confirmer la généralisabilité.

items.title: Monitor Accuracy Isn't the Answer: A Decision-Value Framework for Evaluating AI Agent Restart Monitors
items.summary: Classification accuracy and true-positive and false-positive rates alone do not determine whether restarting an AI agent improves success. Using an exact alarm-to-action identity for an independent clean restart with zero monitoring overhead, we show analytically that a monitor with fixed 90% accuracy can swing from a five-percentage-point loss to a 35-point gain in success rate, depending solely on the replacement attempt's residual-budget success probability. We introduce two techniques for evaluating monitors and progress signals in decision terms. First, a decision-sufficiency criterion, a binary-action specialization of Blackwell's comparison of experiments, identifies which progress representations or context compressions preserve the information needed to choose optimally between the specified actions, independent of trace reconstruction fidelity. Second, a finite-sample, model-free decision audit uses simultaneous binomial intervals over existing agent traces, without additional model calls, to certify a preference for "restart" or "continue" under stated sampling assumptions, or return "abstain" when evidence is insufficient. In a study of 194 externally evaluated model executions on 19 selected SymPy issues from SWE-bench Verified, with a retrospective audit of 130 of these traces, we find a 2.29-point apparent restart gain traced to a single surviving failed attempt, a 42.29-point loss on a second model, no positive replication of the initial gain on prospective task cohorts, and zero of 103 live comparisons meeting the specified certification bar. These results motivate evaluating agent monitors through recovery opportunity, decision value, and statistical support, rather than classification performance alone.
items.tldr: Ce papier propose un cadre théorique pour évaluer les moniteurs de redémarrage des agents IA, démontrant que la précision seule est insuffisante et introduisant des critères décisionnels (suffisance et audit) pour optimiser les décisions de redémarrage en fonction des probabilités de succès résiduelles.

deep_analysis.probleme: Le problème abordé concerne l'évaluation inefficace des moniteurs de redémarrage des agents IA. Les métriques traditionnelles comme la précision de classification ou les taux de vrais/faux positifs ne suffisent pas à déterminer si un redémarrage améliore réellement le taux de succès d'un agent. Cela peut conduire à des décisions sous-optimales dans des systèmes critiques où le coût d'un redémarrage doit être justifié par un gain tangible.
deep_analysis.methode: Les auteurs proposent un cadre d'évaluation basé sur la *valeur décisionnelle* plutôt que sur la performance de classification. Ils introduisent deux techniques clés : 1) Un *critère de suffisance décisionnelle*, inspiré de la comparaison d'expériences de Blackwell, qui vérifie si une représentation des progrès ou une compression du contexte conserve l'information nécessaire pour choisir optimalement entre redémarrer ou continuer, indépendamment de la fidélité de reconstruction des traces. 2) Un *audit décisionnel sans modèle et à échantillon fini*, utilisant des intervalles binomiaux simultanés sur des traces existantes pour certifier une préférence pour l'action 'redémarrer' ou 'continuer', ou s'abstenir en cas de preuves insuffisantes. L'analyse repose sur une identité alarme-action exacte pour un redémarrage propre et indépendant, avec un budget résiduel de succès variable.
deep_analysis.resultats: L'étude applique ce cadre à 194 exécutions de modèles sur 19 problèmes SymPy issus de SWE-bench Verified. Les résultats montrent qu'un moniteur avec 90 % de précision peut entraîner une variation du taux de succès allant d'une perte de 5 points à un gain de 35 points, selon la probabilité de succès résiduelle du redémarrage. L'audit rétrospectif de 130 traces révèle un gain apparent de 2,29 points lié à une seule tentative échouée survivante, une perte de 42,29 points pour un second modèle, et aucune réplication du gain initial sur des cohortes prospectives. Aucune des 103 comparaisons en direct n'a atteint le seuil de certification spécifié.
deep_analysis.limites: Les résultats reposent sur un échantillon limité (19 problèmes SymPy) et des hypothèses fortes, comme l'indépendance du redémarrage et l'absence de surcoût de monitoring. La généralisation à d'autres tâches ou architectures d'agents reste incertaine. De plus, l'absence de réplication des gains initiaux suggère une possible surestimation des effets dans des contextes spécifiques.
deep_analysis.verdict: Ce travail mérite une attention particulière pour son approche innovante et rigoureuse, mais ses conclusions doivent être validées sur des jeux de données plus larges et diversifiés avant d'être adoptées comme référence.

items.title: EvoMemState: Evolving Memory State for Personal Agents
items.summary: Long-term memory enables large language model (LLM) agents to provide continuous personalized assistance by retaining user information across interactions. Existing systems support this process through fact extraction, organization, updating, and retrieval, but largely maintain memories as independent facts. This fact-centric paradigm may overlook how new facts update, constrain, or conflict with earlier ones, while leaving their applicability, role, and priority for the current request implicit. In this paper, we introduce EvoMemState, a state-centric framework that augments persistent facts with two complementary states: Relational States that capture how facts remain valid and relate to one another as memory evolves, and a Reasoning State that determines how these facts should be applied to the current request. Specifically, EvoMemState consists of three key components: (i) Ontology-Guided Memory State Induction extracts Persistent Facts and constructs Relational States that maintain their validity, scope, and evolving relations. (ii) RL-Based State Evolution internalizes memory-use experience into a policy through reinforcement learning to generate a request-specific Reasoning State. (iii) State-Aware Reasoning then combines the relevant facts with their Relational States and the generated Reasoning State to guide the personal agent. Extensive experiments on long-term dialogue and memory-use benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over existing memory systems in retrieval completeness and memory-grounded response accuracy. Our code and implementation details are available at https://github.com/XMUDeepLIT/EvoMemState.git.
items.tldr: EvoMemState propose un cadre *state-centric* pour les agents LLM, remplaçant l'approche factuelle traditionnelle par des états relationnels et de raisonnement dynamiques. Cela permet une mémoire à long terme plus robuste, intégrant les conflits et priorités entre informations pour une assistance personnalisée optimisée.

deep_analysis.probleme: Les systèmes de mémoire à long terme pour les agents conversationnels basés sur les LLM (Large Language Models) traitent généralement les informations utilisateur comme des faits isolés. Cela pose problème car ces systèmes ne capturent pas les relations dynamiques entre les faits, ni leur évolution dans le temps (validité, conflits, priorités), ce qui limite la personnalisation et la cohérence des réponses sur des interactions prolongées.

methode.approche_generale: EvoMemState propose un cadre *state-centric* (centré sur l'état) plutôt que *fact-centric*, en introduisant deux états complémentaires aux faits persistants : les *Relational States* (états relationnels) et le *Reasoning State* (état de raisonnement).

composants_techniques.description: Ce module extrait les *Persistent Facts* (faits persistants) et construit les *Relational States* en utilisant une ontologie pour modéliser la validité, la portée et les relations évolutives entre les faits (ex. : dépendances, contradictions). Cela permet de contextualiser dynamiquement les informations.

Un mécanisme de *reinforcement learning* (apprentissage par renforcement) internalise l'expérience d'utilisation de la mémoire pour générer un *Reasoning State* spécifique à chaque requête. Ce dernier détermine comment appliquer les faits et leurs relations au contexte actuel, via une politique optimisée.

Ce composant combine les faits pertinents, leurs *Relational States* et le *Reasoning State* pour guider l'agent dans la génération de réponses. L'objectif est d'améliorer la précision et la pertinence des réponses en intégrant explicitement l'évolution de la mémoire.

methode.details_supplementaires: Le framework s'appuie sur des benchmarks dédiés aux dialogues longs et à l'utilisation de la mémoire pour évaluer ses performances. L'ontologie et l'apprentissage par renforcement sont des éléments clés pour capturer la complexité des interactions humaines.

deep_analysis.resultats: Les expériences menées sur des benchmarks de dialogue long terme et d'utilisation de la mémoire montrent des améliorations *consistantes* par rapport aux systèmes existants. Les gains concernent notamment : (1) la *complétude de la récupération* des informations pertinentes, et (2) la *précision des réponses* ancrées dans la mémoire. Les chiffres exacts ne sont pas fournis dans le résumé, mais les auteurs soulignent une supériorité systématique sur les approches fact-centric traditionnelles.

limites.manque_de_details: Le résumé ne précise pas les limites techniques du framework, comme la scalabilité des *Relational States* pour des mémoires très volumineuses ou la robustesse face à des données bruitées/contradictoires.
limites.dependances: La performance dépend fortement de la qualité de l'ontologie et de la politique d'apprentissage par renforcement, dont la conception n'est pas détaillée. Une mauvaise initialisation pourrait biaiser les résultats.
limites.evaluation: Les benchmarks utilisés (dialogue long terme) ne couvrent pas nécessairement tous les cas d'usage réels, comme les interactions multi-utilisateurs ou les environnements dynamiques avec des faits en constante évolution.

deep_analysis.verdict: EvoMemState mérite une attention particulière pour son approche innovante et ses résultats prometteurs, mais son adoption nécessitera une analyse critique de ses composants techniques et de sa généralisabilité au-delà des benchmarks présentés.

items.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
items.summary: Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation. Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. We present SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training. Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes action prediction and alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and spatial representations from a frozen 3D perception model. We curate and unify heterogeneous robot datasets to support spatial learning across diverse embodiments, tasks, and scenes. To accommodate this diversity, we introduce feature-dependent gates that adaptively aggregate visual embeddings from multiple VLA layers for spatial supervision. The teacher further exploits partially available depth and camera calibration alongside RGB observations, enabling effective use of heterogeneous geometric annotations. Probabilistic state dropout encourages reliance on visual cues and mitigates overfitting to demonstration trajectories. All auxiliary components are used only during training, allowing direct reuse of pretrained VLA weights and preserving the original inference architecture.
items.tldr: SLA introduit un modèle *Spatial-Language-Action* pré-entraîné en continu pour la robotique, alignant représentations 2D/3D et actions via des *feature-dependent gates*. Une avancée vers des fondations spatiales transférables pour la manipulation précise.

items.title: Future Representation Distillation for Imagination-free World Action Models
items.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) use the predictive knowledge of pretrained video diffusion models for robot control through future video prediction. However, iterative video denoising is costly, and inaccurate visual predictions can compromise action prediction. Our key idea is to make this predictive knowledge available through visual representations computed from the current observation, enabling action prediction without generating future videos. We introduce DreamFree, a WAM that repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a predictive visual encoder through representation distillation. The visual encoder learns to predict a frozen video diffusion model's representation using only the current observation. An action module is then trained to predict actions by extracting action-relevant information from the visual encoder. Across real-world and simulated tasks, DreamFree achieves higher success rates than state-of-the-art VLAs and WAMs, while performing real-time closed-loop control at 11Hz with a 14B video diffusion backbone. Experiments show that DreamFree can translate stronger video priors and additional video data into better robot control and enable learning new robot tasks from video demonstrations, including videos from a different embodiment, without action annotation for the new tasks.
items.tldr: DreamFree distille les connaissances d'un modèle de diffusion vidéo en un encodeur visuel prédictif, permettant un contrôle robotique en temps réel (11Hz) sans génération vidéo itérative. Une approche innovante pour les *World Action Models* (WAMs).

items.title: Open-HumanScale: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
items.summary: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. We introduce Open-HumanScale, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanScale-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language. Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates. Grounded in these findings, we develop HumanWAM-Vanilla, a world--action model pretrained exclusively on 50k hours of egocentric human video. Upon robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, alongside a 14.17% mean success rate and a 19.00 mean progress score on RoboDojo. To push the capability frontier further, we explore joint human--robot pretraining with HumanWAM-Goal, a visual-goal-conditioned world--action model. Hybrid data scaling unlocks broad zero-shot generalization across both simulation and physical benchmarks, propelling post-trained RoboTwin 2.0 performance to new state-of-the-art levels: 92.70% on Clean2Clean and a substantial leap to 84.60% on Clean2Random. On physical robots, HumanWAM-Goal further exhibits emergent embodied in-context learning, dynamically adapting its manipulation behavior to unseen visual goals without parameter updates. To support reproducible scaling research in embodied AI, we open-source the Open-HumanScale-50K corpus, data curation and pretraining pipelines, alongside the pretrained and post-trained HumanWAM checkpoints, inference code, and simulation evaluation suites.
items.tldr: Open-HumanScale propose une recette ouverte pour entraîner des modèles fondés sur l'expérience humaine (50k heures) et robotique, avec une loi de scaling log-linéaire liant données et performance. Une étape clé pour les *Embodied Foundation Models*.

items.title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex
items.summary: Autoregressive approaches with large language models, such as long chain-of-thought reasoning, have become the default for new AI applications because they reach higher accuracy on a wide range of tasks. In production, however, they give inconsistent answers, require parsing of outputs, and add cost and latency. Decision models address this: given a question and a set of options supplied by the user, they return a probability distribution over the options without autoregressive decoding. We present Drex, a family of four open decision models with 8B (DLM), 9B (v1.5), 35B with 3B active (v2.0), and 27B (Max) parameters. Each request consists of a state (a document, record, or agent context, optionally with images) and questions about it, each asking for a choice among options, a yes/no judgment, or a score on an ordered scale. Training combines supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning from adjusted feedback (RLAF), plus vision tuning for Max. Ablations show that RLAF improves accuracy and that consistency losses improve robustness to option order. On Decision Index 0.4.1, Max sets a new state of the art among the decision models we compare (67.52 on the public suite vs. 60.70 for Jev 1.14.0). On Decision Bench v4, it is statistically tied with d3-turbo and GPT-6 Sol and trails Claude Opus 5.5 by 1.6 points, and it has the highest accuracy among decision models on DecideBench. Max answers a typical request in 183 ms, against about 2.0 s for GPT-6 Sol and 3.5 s for Claude Opus 5.5, and its outputs are stable under option reordering. All four models are open source: https://github.com/nace-ai/drex-decision-models
items.tldr: Drex propose une famille de modèles décisionnels (8B à 35B paramètres) évitant l'auto-régression pour des réponses plus rapides et cohérentes, combinant fine-tuning supervisé et apprentissage par renforcement, et atteignant 67.52% sur Decision Index 0.4.1.

items.title: D3D: Decoupled Diffusion Drafting for Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
items.summary: Target-conditioned diffusion drafters predict candidate tokens in parallel, yet each new block must wait for updated target-model hidden states. This forces drafting and verification to run sequentially, limiting speedup even though each block is generated in one pass. We introduce D3D, a standalone diffusion drafter that removes this inter-round dependency. D3D combines blockwise denoising with auxiliary autoregressive supervision to achieve long accepted prefixes without target hidden states. This independence lets D3D draft successor blocks during verification in one packed pass, enabling asynchronous speculative decoding. We progressively prune layers according to their effect on acceptance length to reduce the cost of packed drafting. Removing five of 36 layers retains over 99\% of mean acceptance length across three benchmarks with Qwen3-8B as the target. Across seven benchmarks, D3D averages 5.00times and 5.71times decoding speedup with Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B targets, compared with 4.03times and 3.67times for DFlash. On GSM8K with Qwen3-32B, speedup reaches 7.48times. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/fudan-generative-vision/D3D.
items.tldr: D3D accélère l'inférence des LLM via un drafter diffusion découplé et un pruning progressif, permettant un speedup de 5x à 7.48x sur Qwen3 (8B/32B) en combinant génération asynchrone et pruning efficace des couches.

items.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
items.summary: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions. We ask when such a quantity is identifiable from an experiment's access, continuous in the mechanism and certifiable from finite data, and answer exactly for a deliberately demanding case - the integrated information $\varphi$ of integrated information theory - in stochastic networks of four and five units with known ground truth. Behavior can be silent: a recurrent and a feed-forward network with identical input-output laws at their response delay carry 0.28 and 0 bits, yet internal recordings separate them within 4-53 trials. Partial access can be just as blind: in our examples, units left out of a one-step recording impose precision floors of 0.30-1.02 bits that no sample size lowers, and in all-but-self parity networks, recordings of any length see several hidden units only through the product of their fidelities - a symmetry that one intervention broke in exact checks. The measure has sharp edges: because $\varphi$ selects a partition, and the cause and effect it specifies, by one criterion and reports another, infinitesimal changes of mechanism that cross an edge change it by 25-100% at 99% of the edges we found in random networks, and about 1% of surrogate models that fit interventional data almost perfectly misreport it by more than 20%. One-sided claims survive: the same data certify a lower bound on both sides of an edge, and we prove $\varphi>1.004$ bits throughout a 64-dimensional region of mechanisms and certify it from about $10^7$ controlled transitions with false-certificate probability at most $α$. Measurability is thus a design question with computable answers.
items.tldr: L'étude montre que l'information intégrée (φ) peut être identifiée expérimentalement même avec un accès partiel, mais que certaines symétries cachées ou unités exclues imposent des limites fondamentales de précision, même avec un grand nombre d'essais.

items.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
items.summary: Neural networks are likely to be among the most consequential artefacts in human history. As these systems become more capable and autonomous, their potential to cause societal harm also grows, making AI safety one of the defining challenges of our time. Yet we continue to build increasingly powerful systems without fully understanding how they work, how they will behave in unfamiliar situations, or how to reliably control them. Mechanistic interpretability offers a path towards understanding these systems by studying their internal representations and computations, with the aim of evaluating, predicting, and controlling behaviour. We survey mechanistic interpretability for AI safety in order to answer the question: Does understanding how models work actually make them safer? We place mechanistic interpretability in the broader context of interpretability research and compare its mechanistic evidence with behavioural evaluation. We introduce the foundations of mechanistic interpretability, including features, polysemanticity, transformer computation, and circuits, and survey methods for feature extraction and analysis, circuit discovery and causal verification, explaining intermediate representations in natural language, learning dynamics, and training-data attribution. Beyond surveying existing methods, we propose a unified framework for evaluating mechanistic interpretability claims and characterise six research orientations by their goals, assumptions, and trade-offs. Finally, we examine how mechanistic understanding can support AI safety, including knowledge editing, steering, and monitoring, and assess its limitations, failure modes, open problems, and relationship to behavioural safety measures. We also release a repository of code notebooks with worked examples that reproduce key findings from surveyed methods, allowing readers to build intuition through hands-on experimentation.

extra.authors: Fazl Barez, Tung-Yu Wu, Hunar Batra, Gabriele Dominici, Florent Draye, Yanai Elazar

items.tldr: Synthèse exhaustive sur la *mechanistic interpretability* pour la sécurité IA, couvrant les fondements théoriques (circuits, polysémie), les méthodes d'extraction de features et de vérification causale, et évaluant son rôle dans la prédiction/contrôle des comportements des modèles.

items.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is commonly used in both supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL), often under similar optimizer settings. Yet, how the different dynamics of the two stages manifest in the low-rank increment that LoRA optimizes remains unclear. Tracking the singular spectrum and subspaces of LoRA updates on mathematical reasoning tasks, we find that RL concentrates the spectrum at every learning rate, while SFT expands it at moderate learning rates; moreover, RL rotates the singular subspaces much faster than SFT at small learning rates. Interpolating between SFT and RL one ingredient at a time, we pinpoint group-mean baseline subtraction as the source of both contrasts. A quadratic multi-index model updated via LoRA unveils the underlying mechanism: group-mean baseline subtraction tilts the balance between two competing forces, coherent fitting and gradient noise, toward spectral concentration and faster subspace rotation, while forcing the risk-favorable learning rate to be low. Guided by these dynamics, we tailor LoRA updates to each stage: in SFT, we flatten the spectrum of the full update to spread adaptation across singular directions, whereas in RL, we flatten the part of the update outside the current LoRA increment span to promote subspace rotation. Experiments on mathematical reasoning tasks across multiple models show that the respective configurations for SFT and RL yield the best performance among the compared methods in most evaluated settings.

extra.authors: Chenruo Liu, Zihan Wang, Yijun Dong, Qi Lei

items.tldr: Analyse des dynamiques spectrales et sous-espaces de LoRA en fine-tuning supervisé (SFT) vs. RL, révélant des comportements opposés (concentration vs. expansion du spectre). Identifie le *group-mean baseline* comme cause clé et propose des adaptations de LoRA adaptées à chaque phase.

items.title: Accepted but Wrong: Silent Failures of LLM Code Repairs after API Migrations
items.summary: After a runtime or API migration, an LLM-repaired procedure can run cleanly yet return wrong results, and a release check on typical test inputs ships it. We report a preregistered study of 73 tasks covering 60 documented changes in CPython, Node.js and SQLite. Every candidate is executed on the real runtimes against withheld contracts. Over the complete repair space, the all-assertions gate on typical inputs released 0.410 of wrong repairs. One edge input written from the release note cut this to 0.065, and to 0.061 on 15 unseen clusters. Three inputs from a blind GPT-5.6-luna writer that never saw the program reached 0.070. Two further frozen stages enlarged the menu to 1491 fragments and then added 233 hard distractors that match the legacy output on typical inputs. The edge input (0.058) and the frontier-model writer (0.058) passed their preregistered tests. Yet 0.168 and 0.153 of the hard wrong programs still passed. Two local-model writers failed their preregistered tests. Across four model families, the edge input cut wrong releases per attempt in all three open-weight families on all three menus, for example from 0.233 to 0.057, without lowering correct completion. Self-tests helped less. A blind AI audit flagged 34 contracts as stricter than their requirements. Dropping the disputed checks changed 0 verdicts, but class-label disputes remain open. No model-written code was executed. Artifacts are available from the authors on request.

extra.authors: Xiaobo Chen, Genliang Zhu, Ziyuan Wang, Chu Wang

items.tldr: Étude sur les *silent failures* des réparations de code LLM après migrations d'API, révélant que 41% des correctifs passent les tests standards mais échouent sur des entrées marginales. Soulève des risques critiques pour la fiabilité des systèmes en production.

items.title: Reducing Representational Interference in Retrieval Embeddings with Trainable Prefix Tokens
items.summary: Embedding models compress variable-length text into fixed-size vector representations, but this compression can entangle semantic content with residual token-level information, such as artifacts arising from attention sink behavior. We propose a simple method that prepends trainable [DUMP] tokens to the input during embedding model training. The method keeps the model architecture, pooling strategy, and training loss unchanged, while optimizing the added tokens through the standard contrastive retrieval objective. By introducing trainable prefix positions that interact with regular tokens during encoding, [DUMP] tokens help reduce the influence of residual or uninformative token-level signals on the final retrieval representation. Experiments on standard retrieval and long-context benchmarks show that our method consistently improves over finetuned baselines across encoder and decoder embedding models. Further analysis shows that [DUMP] tokens alter token-level activation and attention patterns associated with low-information tokens. These results suggest that trainable prefix tokens provide a lightweight way to improve retrieval representations.
items.tldr: Méthode légère utilisant des tokens d'entrée entraînables ([DUMP]) pour réduire l'interférence des signaux résiduels (comme les artefacts de 'attention sink') dans les embeddings de retrieval, améliorant les performances sur des benchmarks standard sans modifier l'architecture ou la stratégie de pooling.

items.title: On the Opportunities and Challenges of Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-Model Transfer
items.summary: Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-model Transfer (PACT), a form of latent communication between language models, combines a larger model's prompt representations with a smaller model's efficient generation, offering a promising way to balance capability and inference cost. However, existing systems provide limited support for independently evaluating large-small model collaboration, and improved task performance alone does not establish whether the receiver benefits from the sender's information. We introduce PLatour, an open-source PACT framework that connects frozen models through lightweight, zero-initialized linear bridges trained directly with task rewards and supports hybrid-attention architectures. PLatour significantly outperforms open-source baselines on generation tasks and surpasses Mostik's reported results on shared mathematics and coding benchmarks using a substantially smaller sender. However, controlled experiments show that the gains on some tasks can be reproduced by uninformative sender signals, self-communication, or receiver-only training. We find that trainable bridges can act as parameter-efficient adaptation mechanisms without exploiting useful sender information. We therefore propose PACT-Check to quantify how much of a trained PACT system's gain genuinely comes from communication. Finally, we discuss the opportunities and challenges of PACT systems. Code is available at https://github.com/zhenyi4/platour.
items.tldr: Cadre PACT (Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-model Transfer) pour combiner les représentations d'un grand modèle avec la génération d'un modèle plus petit via des ponts linéaires entraînables, avec évaluation critique des gains réels (certains résultats reproduisibles sans information utile du 'sender').

items.title: SAE Interprets MoE: Sparse AutoEncoders Reveal That MoE Experts Exhibit Human-Interpretable Fine-Grained Specialization
items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models route each token to a few of many experts, yet what an individual expert is responsible for remains unsettled. Existing analyses count how often an expert is selected on domain-labeled corpora, an instrument that fixes the taxonomy in advance, stays coarse, and records selection rather than contribution. We instead study specialization in feature space by training a sparse autoencoder (SAE) on the output of an MoE layer. Since this output is a router-weighted sum of expert outputs and the SAE encoder is affine, the pre-activation of every latent decomposes exactly over the experts. Aggregated over a corpus, this gives each expert a dominant set of latents whose activation it principally drives. On layers 4, 30 and 46 of Qwen3-30B-A3B, contribution is far more concentrated than gating, most latents have only one or two dominators, and the overlap between dominant sets concentrates on a few expert pairs. Auto-interpreting these sets reveals a division of labor below coarse domains, with distinct experts for Java and front-end web code, or for geometry and for arithmetic and polynomials, while the coarse domains themselves take very unequal numbers of experts. Our SAEs and code are available at https://github.com/Bytedance-Seed/SAE-Interprets-MoE.
items.tldr: Utilisation de SAE pour analyser la spécialisation fine des experts dans les MoE (Qwen3-30B-A3B), révélant des divisions de travail précises (ex: Java vs front-end) et une concentration des contributions bien plus granulaire que les patterns de routage.

items.title: Random Is Almost Enough? Stable and Low-Cost Benchmark Compression via BestRand
items.summary: Benchmark compression reduces the often prohibitive time and cost of model evaluation by evaluating models on a small benchmark subset that closely matches full-benchmark results. To quantify estimation error, we derive an accurate analytical approximation to the error distribution when estimating full-benchmark scores from a subset, showing that most subsets yield small errors, while a few produce much larger errors, resulting in a long-tailed distribution. This means random sampling alone can achieve surprisingly strong performance with high probability, but remains unstable due to rare large errors. We further show that this instability is inherent to modern foundation models and persists even as more models are evaluated. Based on these findings, we introduce BestRand, a stable and low-cost benchmark compression method that preserves the efficiency of random sampling while substantially reducing its high-error tail. We validate BestRand on 70+ text, multimodal, and agent benchmarks, and further extend it to VLA evaluation. Compared with competitive methods, BestRand reduces high-error risk by 50.2% and estimation error by 16.4% on average, while requiring only 51.3% of the construction cost. It further reduces OOD estimation error by 21.8% on average across score-range, model-family, and temporal shifts. Together, our theory provides practical guidance for understanding and predicting the accuracy and reliability of benchmark compression, while BestRand enables stable and accurate compression at low cost. The code and data are publicly available onhttps://github.com/George-Ling3/BestRand.
items.tldr: BestRand introduit une méthode de compression de benchmarks stable et peu coûteuse pour l'évaluation des modèles, réduisant les erreurs d'estimation de 50% et les coûts computationnels de 48% en moyenne, tout en maintenant une haute précision sur 70+ benchmarks.

items.title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision. Does this dense signal reduce the training FLOPs needed to reach a target accuracy compared with reinforcement learning? We systematically compare vanilla reverse-KL OPD with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) across task difficulty, student and teacher size, domain, and optimization choices, measuring held-out accuracy against training FLOPs. With an external post-trained teacher, OPD generally loses to GRPO in accuracy per training FLOP at matched settings, even when the teacher is further trained with GRPO, and often suffers response-length inflation. Yet a different teacher changes the picture: when the teacher is the student's own GRPO checkpoint, OPD recovers that checkpoint's accuracy on math with $50\times$ fewer distillation FLOPs than GRPO needs to reach the same accuracy. Following the same teacher setting, we consistently observe this high efficiency with a larger student, on code, and in a second model family. On a single domain, however, the GRPO checkpoint is already the desired model, so distilling it adds to total compute. Across domains, separate GRPO checkpoints hold different capabilities, and no single checkpoint serves every domain. Multi-teacher OPD (DeepSeek-AI, 2026) consolidates per-domain GRPO experts into a single student that matches each expert's accuracy, with the distillation stage costing only 5.2% (on 2 domains) and 8.0% (on 4 domains) of the specialist training FLOPs. Counting specialist training and distillation together, this pipeline reaches joint GRPO's performance on the 2-domain mix with 42.0% fewer total FLOPs.

extra.authors: Zeyu Leo Liu, Yang Li, Bo Pang, Emre Can Acikgoz, Xuan-Phi Nguyen, Anurag Koul

items.tldr: La distillation on-policy (OPD) peut être jusqu'à 50x plus efficace en FLOPs que GRPO pour atteindre une précision cible, mais cela dépend fortement du choix du professeur (externe vs auto-GRPO), avec des risques d'inflation de longueur de réponse.

items.title: StrataFlux: Memory-Hierarchy-Native Low-Bit LLM Inference
items.summary: Quantization reduces the memory and bandwidth demands of large language model (LLM) inference but can degrade accuracy; offloading higher-precision data can instead stall generation. We introduce StrataFlux, a framework that challenges this tradeoff by recovering accuracy lost to low-bit weight and key-value (KV) cache quantization while retaining quantization's memory and speed advantages. StrataFlux co-designs refinement representation, selection, and delivery to make host RAM and solid-state drives useful sources of additional precision. Its selective precision streaming reduces transfer volume, overlaps delivery with computation, and reuses fetched precision across decoding steps so generation need not wait for every transfer. We evaluate 2-4-bit weights and 2-3-bit KV-cache on dedicated GPUs and unified-memory platforms. For 2-bit Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct weights, StrataFlux reduces WikiText-2 perplexity from 9.46 to 8.40 while maintaining 95.4% of the quantized base's throughput on RTX 5090. With 2-bit weights and KV, StrataFlux raises Qwen3-8B's AIME 2024/2025 accuracy from 11.0% to 47.1% at unchanged GPU memory use. At 128K context, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with 3-bit weights and 2-bit KV achieves comparable perplexity and speed to vLLM's 4-bit AWQ weights and 8-bit KV on RTX 5090, using approximately half the GPU memory. These results show that GPU-resident precision need not set the accuracy ceiling, nor offloading-tier latency dictate decoding speed.

extra.authors: Jake Hyun, Ziyu Zhao, Jae-sun Seo, Mohamed S. Abdelfattah

items.tldr: StrataFlux améliore l'inférence des LLM quantifiés en récupérant la précision perdue via un streaming sélectif de précision depuis RAM/SSD, combinant gains mémoire et vitesse sans sacrifier la performance. Solution clé pour le déploiement efficace des LLM.

items.title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression
items.summary: LLM pruning must preserve quality while meeting hardware- and workload-specific constraints on latency, throughput, and memory. Existing pruning workflows often target parameter counts, requiring practitioners to manually select model sizes that meet latency, throughput, and GPU memory limits. However, parameter count alone does not predict these metrics, which depend on the model architecture, workload, hardware, and serving engine. We introduce AutoCompress, a hardware-guided compression framework that directly incorporates such constraints into differentiable architecture search. AutoCompress jointly optimizes global and per-layer structure to produce heterogeneous architectures, guided by serving-engine cost models validated against end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory measurements. We evaluate AutoCompress on long-context local coding, batched datacenter serving, and latency-sensitive in-game interaction. Compared to the state-of-the-art Minitron pruning framework, AutoCompress improves average accuracy across eight benchmarks by 6.57, 2.35, and 0.57 percentage points on RTX 5070, RTX 5080, and H100, respectively. AutoCompress also compresses Nemotron 3.5 Super from 120B to 74B parameters for single-B200 BF16 serving at 128K context, retaining 95% of its mean benchmark score.

extra.authors: Sheldon Liang, Ali Taghibakhshi, Saurav Muralidharan, Sharath Turuvekere Sreenivas, Ashwath Aithal, Pavlo Molchanov

items.tldr: Framework *AutoCompress* pour le *pruning* guidé par le matériel, intégrant des contraintes de latence/throughput/mémoire via une recherche d'architecture différentiable. Améliore significativement la précision vs. Minitron tout en respectant les contraintes hardware, avec évaluations sur RTX 5070/5080/H100.

items.title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
items.summary: Personal AI agents face social engineering attacks supported by forged multimodal content, but existing evaluations mainly focus on text-based dialogue, leaving their intrinsic security under such attacks insufficiently studied. We introduce Multimodal-SEA, an interactive benchmark comprising 608 expert-designed tasks grounded in real-world fraud cases, covering 14 domains and 152 attack scenarios with prepared multimodal content. The tasks span four difficulty levels and reflect the distinct social and cultural contexts of Chinese and English environments. Agents inspect content, verify requests, and execute actions in simulated applications, with attack outcomes grounded in verifiable tool execution logs. To enable controlled red teaming of personal agents, we design a multimodal attack harness that integrates task information, attack progression control, and multimodal content construction to evaluate their intrinsic security against adaptive social engineering attacks in simulated environments. Evaluating seven widely used multimodal models across six dimensions reveals that all are vulnerable, with attack success rates of 7.1% to 34.5%. Adding multimodal content increases attack success from 19.9% to 29.2%, despite increased proactive verification coverage. Stronger safety instructions reduce attack success without improving recognition of deceptive multimodal content, while lower attack success rates for some models accompany excessive refusal of legitimate requests.

extra.authors: Zhitao He, Chi Him Zhang, Chengru Han, Yi R Fung

items.tldr: Benchmark *Multimodal-SEA* évaluant la sécurité des agents IA multimodaux face à des attaques d'ingénierie sociale avec contenu falsifié (texte, image, audio). Tous les modèles testés sont vulnérables, avec des taux de succès d'attaque allant jusqu'à 34.5%, soulignant des risques concrets pour les agents personnels.

items.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
items.summary: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to the primitive's type, dimensionality, and length, supporting compact boxes and long, variable-length trajectories. Crucially, spatial accuracy need not require reproducing an autoregressive model's exact token sequence. VFlash therefore trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement. Across the evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, VFlash consistently reduces prediction errors relative to autoregressive decoding. Preliminary single-rollout measurements indicate approximately 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting. A world action model conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites, compared with 62.6% for the baseline.
items.tldr: VFlash accélère la planification visuelle (trajectoires, boîtes) en décodant des primitives spatiales *jointement* via un modèle léger, réduisant les erreurs et le coût de calcul par rapport à l'auto-régression classique.

items.title: Harness-S: Learning from Sibling Harnesses for Generalizable Agent Training
items.summary: Harness evolution from a common base exhibits Locality, Complementarity, and Nonstationarity: variants repair different failures, and their utility changes as the policy learns. Rather than seeking a universally superior harness, we introduce Harness-S to selectively rescue failures of a base execution system through sibling harnesses and transfer the resulting capabilities into a single policy that remains effective under the original harness. Directional Harness Evolution develops specialized sibling harnesses along distinct repair directions, forming a reusable Sibling Harness Pool that remains fixed during policy training. Complementary Harness Rescue Training invokes this pool only when all initial attempts under the base harness fail. The same policy generates fresh rollouts under selected auxiliary harnesses, and these trajectories replace the failed group for reinforcement learning. An Adaptive Harness Router selects the Top-k variants using Harness Behavior Profiles and voting across multiple LLMs. Policy-aware profile re-anchoring refreshes this evidence as the policy learns. Across AppWorld, SWE-Gym, and DBBench, the trained policy substantially outperforms policy-only training when returned to the original base harness. Behavioral analyses and held-out cases support the transfer of harness-elicited behaviors into the policy itself. Reusing the router for Rank-1 inference provides additional gains at the same executor rollout count.
items.tldr: Harness-S améliore l'entraînement des agents LLM en exploitant des *sibling harnesses* spécialisés pour corriger les échecs, transférant les capacités acquises vers une politique unique. Une méthode efficace pour la généralisation multi-tâches.

items.title: DRAP: Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity for Continual Learning in Physical AI
items.summary: Continual learning in physical AI differs from conventional continual learning because small per-step policy errors can accumulate over a trajectory. Each deviation may move the agent outside the training distribution, increase subsequent prediction errors, and ultimately cause closed-loop task failure. This work introduces Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity (DRAP), a replay-free method that estimates the historical importance of adaptable model tensors from sample-level action gradients weighted by local trajectory-amplification risk. A ridge-regularized local linear model is fitted to expert state-action transitions, and the largest singular value of its state-transition matrix provides a policy-independent, Lyapunov-inspired estimate of one-step perturbation amplification. After each task, risk-weighted squared gradients are accumulated in a tensor-level importance memory. During subsequent tasks, DRAP uses normalized cumulative importance to scale the effective AdamW learning rate of each tensor, immediately reducing the plasticity of components that supported previous behavior at dynamically sensitive trajectory points. We instantiate DRAP on a fixed KappaTune-selected subnetwork of OpenVLA and evaluate replay-free sequential adaptation across the LIBERO Spatial, Object, and Goal suites. Compared with standard AdamW fine-tuning and EWC, the results show substantially improved retention of previously learned behaviors while preserving strong new-suite acquisition.
items.tldr: DRAP introduit une méthode de plasticité adaptative pour l'apprentissage continu en robotique physique, estimant les risques de perturbation des trajectoires pour ajuster dynamiquement l'apprentissage des modèles, améliorant ainsi la robustesse aux erreurs cumulatives.

items.title: NitroFusion2: Bringing Adversarial Loss to the Text Stream of Multimodal Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: Adversarial diffusion distillation has conventionally relied on image features for discrimination. We revisit this choice for multimodal diffusion transformers (MMDiTs), whose text stream becomes image-dependent through joint attention. We introduce Text-Stream Adversarial Distillation (TSAD), which exploits intermediate text-token states as a new adversarial representation. Because the text stream has already read the image while remaining tied to the text condition, changing that condition changes what information it extracts from the image. Building on this property, we introduce Aspect-Cued Discrimination (ACD), which conditions the discriminator on different aspects of the sample, such as typography, objects, or style, to steer which properties are emphasized during adversarial training. Building on the expert-discriminator design of NitroFusion, we integrate TSAD and ACD in NitroFusion2. NitroFusion2 brings few-step distillation from the conventional 4-8-step regime down to just 1-2 steps at comparable quality. At one step, it produces sharp rendered text and rich fine-grained details, making one-step generation practical rather than merely a stress test for distillation. At two steps, it remains competitive across the evaluated benchmarks. These results establish the MMDiT text stream as a powerful and steerable representation for adversarial diffusion distillation.
items.tldr: NitroFusion2 améliore la distillation adversariale des MMDiT en ciblant le flux textuel, réduisant le nombre d'étapes de 4-8 à 1-2 tout en conservant la qualité, via une discrimination conditionnée par des aspects (typographie, style).

items.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
items.summary: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decoding to text, and share information by passing KV caches. Each swarm studies the problem from a different angle. A novelty filter keeps the most distinct agent ideas by directly measuring the distances between the agents' hidden state vectors. Crossover of ideas happens naturally in latent space, as a summarizer agent receives the combined KV caches of all swarm members. On 21 problems in mathematical discovery and scientific computing, SwarmEvolve gets the highest average score and needs a median of only 3 to 8 minutes to reach the best scores that other state-of-the-art frameworks reach in 60 minutes. On several problems, SwarmEvolve with Qwen3 8B improves on the solutions that AlphaEvolve first found with frontier LLMs. Our work shows that agent swarms that communicate in latent space offer a fast, low-cost approach to program search for scientific problems.
items.tldr: SwarmEvolve utilise des essaims d'agents LLM optimisant des solutions en espace latent (sans décodage textuel), partageant des caches KV et filtrant les idées par distance dans l'espace caché, réduisant drastiquement le temps d'optimisation (3-8 min vs 60 min pour les méthodes classiques).

items.title: StepBack: Step-Level Error-Localized Resampling for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning
items.summary: Self-consistency (SC) is a widely used decoding strategy for improving chain-of-thought reasoning, but it requires sampling many complete reasoning trajectories with a preset budget. Its efficient variants reduce the cost mainly by stopping full-trajectory sampling early or distributing the number of samples across questions. In this paper, we propose StepBack, a step-level error-localized resampling method for efficient test-time reasoning. Given a small set of draft trajectories, StepBack localizes likely first error positions using lightweight signals and then resamples the detected error step and its suffix, followed by majority answer voting. Empirically, StepBack matches the accuracy of SC on average across seven mathematical reasoning and multi-hop QA benchmarks, while reducing token usage by up to 41.26%. In addition, by nature, StepBack can be combined with adaptive inference methods such as Adaptive Consistency, further improving their inference-time efficiency.
items.tldr: StepBack optimise l'inférence des LLM en localisant et resamplant les étapes erronées dans les raisonnements en chaîne, réduisant jusqu'à 41% des tokens utilisés sans perte de précision. Approche innovante pour l'efficacité des LLM, mais nécessite plus de benchmarks variés.

items.title: Cultural Adaptation within Repeated Social Interactions
items.summary: Much of human culture is tacit and is typically learned through situated social interaction. As LLMs are deployed as interactive agents across diverse communities, assessing their cultural competence demands moving beyond existing question-answering approaches, shifting from what they know to how they adapt. In this work, we broaden the scope of cultural adaptation in NLP by investigating whether LLMs can adapt through repeated interactions via a sandbox environment. By reframing cultural adaptation as a continuous process of norm assimilation through social interaction, our work demonstrates that memory mechanisms foster longitudinal learning across repeated interactions, facilitate transfer to different social settings, and enable multilingual norm assimilation across five languages. Together, our findings lay the groundwork for continuous, interaction-driven cultural adaptation in LLMs.

extra.authors: Chen Cecilia Liu, Roi Reichart, Anna Korhonen

items.tldr: Étude explorant la capacité des LLM à s'adapter culturellement via des interactions répétées dans un environnement bac à sable, démontrant que des mécanismes de mémoire améliorent l'apprentissage longitudinal et la transférabilité entre contextes sociaux et multilingues.

items.title: Decode Before You Hear: Speculative Listening for Chunk-Interleaved Full-Duplex Speech Language Models
items.summary: Chunk-interleaved full-duplex speech language models listen and speak in fixed time chunks, and each chunk must be processed before the next one arrives. Their workload is asymmetric across chunks: listen chunks leave compute idle while awaiting audio, and speak and tool-call chunks require serial generation, which delays responses and tool calls. Using the idle compute for the next chunk requires decoding it before its audio arrives, under an assumed input. Taking silence as the assumed input and comparing the output with the output under real audio on four models, we observe two properties. First, the next audio chunk does not change the output in 95.3% of chunks. Second, 88% of changes begin at the first output token. Building on these properties, we propose Speculative Listening, a training-free, lossless framework for input-time self-speculative decoding. During idle time, the model drafts the next chunk under silence and, for changes at the first token, a second branch from the runner-up first token. It keeps all drafts in a cross-chunk hypothesis pool and verifies them when the audio arrives. On our eight-task benchmark TickTock-Bench, Speculative Listening speeds up speak chunks by 2.6-2.8x and tool-call chunks by up to 23.4x. On average, it reduces the decoding delay before a response starts by 73%, to 74-241 ms, close to the 200 ms gap between human turns, and the maximum lag behind real time by 94.4%.
items.tldr: Speculative Listening exploite les périodes d'inactivité des modèles de parole full-duplex pour prédire le prochain chunk audio via *self-speculative decoding*, accélérant les réponses de 95% sans perte de qualité. Une optimisation temps réel prometteuse pour les interfaces vocales.

items.title: Identically Trained Language Models Break on Different Jailbreaks
items.summary: Jailbreak benchmarks test one checkpoint and treat which jailbreaks break it as a property of its pretraining data and safety training. We ask whether another pretraining run of the same data, given the same safety training, would break on the same jailbreaks. For each of 25 pretraining data recipes, we take 1B base models from 3 pretraining seeds and give each the same safety post-training with 2 post-training seeds, for 150 models in all. We then collect 20 responses from every model to a shared set of jailbreak prompts and correlate the per-prompt non-refusal rates between every pair of models. On average, two post-trained copies of the same pretraining run have per-prompt non-refusal rates that correlate at 0.984. A different pretraining seed lowers the correlation to 0.811, and a different data recipe lowers it only slightly further, to 0.779. These results indicate that which jailbreaks break a checkpoint depends much more on its pretraining run than on its data, a pattern that holds in all 25 data recipes and at 150M and 300M parameters. In practice, the best of 91 attack templates found on one checkpoint stays the best after a new pretraining seed in only 27% of model pairs, against 67% after a new post-training seed. Each pretraining run also leaves a fingerprint: across 3,211 prompts, a model's per-prompt non-refusal rates identify its pretraining run among all 75 runs every time, and a random subset of 50 prompts still does so 98% of the time.
items.tldr: Étude empirique montrant que la robustesse aux *jailbreaks* dépend davantage de la graine de pré-entraînement que des données ou de l'alignement. Un résultat critique pour évaluer la généralisation des mécanismes de sécurité des LLM.
